content.title: Why Hertz (HTZ) Stock Is Up Today
content.summary: Shares of global car rental company Hertz (NASDAQ:HTZ) jumped 39.5% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter financial results that significantly beat Wall Street expectations. The company posted revenue of $2.48 billion, topping estimates, and an adjusted profit of $0.12 per share, which was 83.8% higher than the consensus forecast of $0.07. content.title: Hertz Logs First Profit in Two Years as it Modernizes Fleet, Grows Car Sales
content.summary: Hertz posted its first profit in more than two years as its focus on swapping in newer vehicles and expanding into car sales pays off.  “We’ve transformed our fleet from a headwind to a competitive advantage,” Chief Executive  Gil West  said, adding that the company’s average car age is now under 12 months.  A younger fleet reduces the declines in car value Hertz logs on its balance sheet and improves the fleet’s capacity by cutting down on the time the cars need to be serviced.

content.title: Hertz Stock Surges 37% on Return to Profitability. What’s Driving the Gains.
content.summary: Shares surged more than 37% to $6.83, heading for the largest same-day percentage increase since a 44% jump in April, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  Peer  Avis Budget Group  was up 3.3%.  The recovery was largely due to lower depreciation of Hertz’s assets—in this case, rental cars—as measured in depreciation per unit per month, which fell 49% to $273 in the quarter.
